Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Confirmed tornadoes: This tornado touched down on the west side of Arkadelphia and moved northeastward along the Ouachita River, hitting the south side of Midway before dissipating. Three homes and 13 farm buildings were destroyed while six homes and 16 other buildings were damaged. Some livestock were killed as well. Damages were estimated at $50,000 and three people were injured.[2][3][5]

Confirmed tornadoes: An intense tornado destroyed or damaged a church, a few stores, a large consolidated school building, 30 homes, and many barns. Two of the homes were unroofed as well. Damages were estimated at $250,000 and one person was injured. Tornado researcher Thomas P. Grazulis classified the tornado as an F2.[2][3][6]

Confirmed tornadoes: This strong tornado first touched down on the southwest side of Little Rock in Meadowcliff and passed through Geyer Springs. A drive-in theaterscreen was damaged and two cars in the theater lot were overturned, injuring five people. The tornado then progressed northeastward and struck the residential district, causing considerable damage to roofs before striking the business district of Downtown Little Rock. There was extensive damage to roofs, windows, plate glass, signs, and brick and masonry parapets. A large radio antenna mast toppled from roof of the Gazette Building. The tornado then crossed the Arkansas River into North Little Rock, where it did considerable damage to roofs, trees and signs, and injured two more people. The tornado weakened after that, causing slight crop damage before dissipating west of Booker. Seven people were injured and losses totaled $250,000. Considerable water damage by rain entering buildings through torn roofs and broken windows also occurred as a result of this tornado. Some small hail was also observed as well.[2][3][7]

Confirmed tornadoes: This massive, mile-wide tornado accompanied by moderate hail likely came from the same storm that produced the Little Rock tornado. Timber, farm buildings, farm equipment, and 33 homes were heavily damaged or destroyed and livestock was injured. Minimal crop damage also occurred. Damages were estimated at $250,000 and 20 people were injured. The CDNS report list 15 injuries. Grazulis listed the tornado as an F2.[2][3][8]

Confirmed tornadoes: A strong tornado, which likely came from the same storm that produced the Little Rock and Hickory Plains tornadoes, occurred southeast of Georgetown. A total of seven to 10 homes were heavily damaged or destroyed, of which a few shifted and collapsed on their foundations, and several barns were destroyed as well. Two people were injured, but no damage value was given.[2][3][9]

Confirmed tornadoes: A broom handle factory was obliterated by this funnel-less but strong, southeastward-moving tornado. Local residents were able to identify the damage as tornadic due to the pattern of the debris. Damages were estimated at $2,500. Grazulis did not list the tornado as an F2 or stronger.[2][3][10]
Confirmed tornadoes: 1 death – A couple of barns and six tenant homes were destroyed while one large home was shifted on its foundation. Two people were injured.[2][3][11]

Confirmed tornadoes: A total of 30 tenant homes and an unspecified number of barns were destroyed. Damages were estimated at $25,000 and two people were injured. Grazulis classified the tornado as an F2. This may have been the same tornado that struck Belzoni, Mississippi.[2][3][12]
Confirmed tornadoes: Barns were destroyed and a home was unroofed, although no damage estimate was given.[2][3][13]

Confirmed tornadoes: This was the first of two strong tornadoes to hit Downtown Jackson along similar beginning paths before diverging. It also struck Forest Hill, Bradie, Wells, Meltonville, Cameron and Truitt. Damages were estimated at $500,000 and seven people were injured. Grazulis did not list the tornado as an F2 or stronger.[2][3][14]

Confirmed tornadoes: This was the second of two strong tornadoes to hit Downtown Jackson along similar beginning paths before diverging. It also struck Forest Hill, Bradie, Flowood, Northern Wells, Luckney, and Pisgah. Damages were estimated at $500,000 and six people were injured. Grazulis did not list the tornado as an F2 or stronger.[2][3][15]
Confirmed tornadoes: Damages were estimated at $25,000. The tornado was not listed in the CDNS report.[16]
Confirmed tornadoes: No damage estimate was given. Grazulis did not list the tornado as an F2 or stronger.[2][3][17]

Confirmed tornadoes: A Masonic lodge, two churches, and 24 homes were unroofed, damaged, or destroyed. Damages were estimated at $25,000 and two people were injured. Grazulis classified the tornado as an F2.[2][3][18]
Confirmed tornadoes: A small tornado moved northeastward, damaging buildings, trees, and power and telephone lines. Losses totaled $2,500.[2][19]

Confirmed tornadoes: This strong tornado, which was described as having a 'whitish' colored, funnel, destroyed several outbuildings on one farm and knocked down power lines. Damages were estimated at $2,500. Grazulis did not list the tornado as an F2 or stronger.[2][3][20]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Near the beginning of the path, the roofs of a barn and two houses were damaged. The tornado developed a multi-vortex structure as it passed north of Black, Missouri, where a mobile home was heavily damaged and shifted 30 yd (27.43 m). Farther East, vehicles were tossed up to 50 yd (45.72 m) from where they were parked, and an uninhabited house was completely destroyed. The tornado crossed into Iron County, where five houses sustained roof and exterior damage, and a mobile home was flipped on its side. Two houses also sustained damage from falling trees near Snow Hollow Lake. Near Pilot Knob, a mobile home sustained moderate damage, a machine shed was destroyed, and numerous houses sustained roof damage before the tornado dissipated. Many trees and power poles were snapped along the tornado’s track.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: This violent tornado first destroyed a barn and partially unroofed a two‐story house near Friedenberg, then blew trees onto another house. The tornado unroofed another house as it entered Crosstown, Missouri. Major structural damage occurred with multiple houses and businesses heavily damaged or destroyed. A church and a nearby brick building lost their roofs, vehicles were flipped, and trees were mangled. Four well‐constructed houses were completely leveled, one with only its bolted‐down floor remaining. East of town, the tornado weakened to F3 intensity and destroyed a modular home, leaving only the bathroom standing, and some outbuildings. In Perry County alone, 62 houses were destroyed, 17 had major damage, and 23 sustained only minor damage. The tornado crossed the Mississippi River, pushed a coal barge into the shoreline, and blew out the tugboat's windows. In Illinois, the tornado weakened to F2 intensity, destroyed a mobile home, and tore the roof and wall off a farmhouse. Farther east, a house was unroofed, another had its addition torn off, a swingset was blown and wrapped around a mailbox, an empty tractor-trailer rig was overturned, and an empty grain bin was blown into a field. Near Route 3, a brick house was unroofed, power poles snapped, and large areas of corn flattened. At the Kinkaid Lake marina, about 50 RVs and boats were damaged.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Table – Missouri, F4 row (SE ofPerryvilleto N ofMurphysboro, Illinois, Perry,Jackson (IL), 2107) [28][29]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Header 'Vanuatu': As Cyclone Paula threatened Vanuatu, RSMC Nadi issued a total of 14 special advisories for the island chain at six–hour intervals, beginning at 2344 UTC on February 25 and ending at 0230 UTC on March 1. In the Port Vila area, an estimated 100 families were evacuated from potentially flood‐prone areas. The cyclone caused heavy rainfall and flooding across Vanuatu. Areas in the western parts of Espiritu Santo experienced damage due to strong winds and flooding in low-lying areas, forcing the evacuation of communities to higher ground. Trees were uprooted causing damage to communication lines and power outages. An estimated 45–50% of all houses and gardens were damaged, along with 25% of other infrastructure.

Header 'Fiji': In Fiji's Western Division, strong storm surge destroyed homes in nine villages across the coastline. Root crops, fruit trees, and sugar cane fields were damaged due to Paula. Strong rains resulted in minor landslides and road closures. One fatality was reported in Fiji due to Cyclone Paula.

Total_Summary_Insured_Damage.Total_Insured_Damage_Annotation: Lawsuit header: 'The case was taken to court, and in 1995, the jury awarded the American Samoa Government $28.9 million. Soon after, the amount was doubled to $57.8 million to include punitive damages. The total damages awarded by the judgment was $86.7 million, which the judge stated to be "the largest insurance bad faith verdict in the state of California in 1995".' [3]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Lawsuit header: 'In 1991, American Samoa purchased a $45 million "all risk" insurance policy from the firm Affiliated FM Insurance. The firm would only pay up to $6.1 million for the damages, arguing that the insurance did not cover water damage, only that caused by the wind. Attorney William Shernoff discovered that the policy had been altered to exclude damages caused by "wind-driven water" despite covering cyclones. The case was taken to court, and in 1995, the jury awarded the American Samoa Government $28.9 million, later doubled to $57.8 million for punitive damages, making the total judgment $86.7 million, noted as the largest insurance bad faith verdict in California in 1995.' [3]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: List of confirmed tornadoes - June 11, 1970: 'A tornado touched down in the Bunch area, damaging a mission school, where one injury occurred. Considerable damage also occurred in Stilwell, Oklahoma. The tornado directly hit Springdale, Arkansas, killing William E. Cawthon, 57, at his home just west of town, causing over $1 million (1970 USD) in damages after 138 homes, apartments, and businesses were extensively damaged. A shopping mall was leveled and also a manor. Ground scouring occurred west of the Springdale limits. The communities of Rhea, Lincoln, Wheeler, and Harmon sustained damage to twelve poultry houses. In Rhea, a public building sustained damage and a church was removed from its foundation. Five hen houses were damaged and a boat dock was slightly damaged before the tornado dissipated.'

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: List of confirmed tornadoes - June 12, 1970: 'A violent tornado cut a swath of total destruction from Musselfork to Callao. The first noted damage was to three homes, one mobile home, and several barns, of which all were destroyed. Five homes and 10 barns also suffered extensive damage. A bridge was lifted in the air and dropped upstream, one span length from its original location. The tornado continued its path and either damaged or destroyed outbuildings, barns, and farm machinery on three farms, with lesser damage to five others before dissipating.'

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: One home destroyed; six other homes badly damaged; a nearby building had its roof ripped off; a communication tower toppled; a crane toppled; at least two mobile homes destroyed; several homes lost their roofs; many barns destroyed or badly damaged
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: List of confirmed tornadoes - June 12, 1970: 'An intense tornado touched down in the Macon area, causing intermittent destruction to buildings. One home was destroyed near the starting point of the path, along with six other homes that were badly damaged. On the first house, a rubber welcome mat made an imprint of the word "welcome" on the side of the house. The tornado toppled a communication tower and ripped the roof off of a building nearby. A crane was also toppled where a bridge was being constructed. After exiting Macon, at least two mobile homes were destroyed, several homes lost their roofs, and many barns were destroyed or badly damaged. One person sustained injuries from the tornado.'

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: A few houses sustained roof and exterior damage; one attached garage was completely destroyed; outbuildings were damaged or destroyed.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF1, SE of New Richmond, St. Croix, WI – 'A few houses sustained roof and exterior damage, one of which had its attached garage completely destroyed with debris strewn through a nearby farm field. Outbuildings were damaged or destroyed, and trees were snapped or uprooted.' [11]
EF0, W of Borth, Waushara, WI – 'Crops were flattened and an outbuilding was damaged.' [12][13]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Outbuildings and mobile homes were damaged; storage trailers were thrown and destroyed.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF1, S of Portage, Columbia, WI – 'Trees, outbuildings, and mobile homes were damaged. Storage trailers were thrown and destroyed.' [14]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: A metal roof panel was ripped from a barn (resulting in roof damage to that structure).
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF1, SE of Cross Plains, Dane, WI (Cross Plains 2) – 'Trees were snapped or uprooted, and tree limbs were downed. Crop damage occurred, and a metal roof panel was ripped from a barn and thrown into a field.' [17]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: A few homes sustained minor shingle damage; a house under construction sustained collapse of its roof and exterior walls; a garage door was damaged.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF1, West Middleton, Dane, WI (Middleton) – 'Many trees and tree limbs were downed in West Middleton, a few of which landed on homes. A garage door was also damaged by flying tree debris. Homes sustained minor shingle damage, and a house that was under construction sustained collapse of its roof and exterior walls.' [18]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Houses had fascia and gutters ripped off; an apartment building had shingles torn from its roof.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF0, Northern Verona, Dane, WI (Verona) – 'A tornado moved through the northern part of Verona, downing trees and tree branches. One large but rotten tree trunk was snapped, a basketball hoop was blown over, and houses had fascia and gutters ripped off. Shingles were torn from the roof of an apartment building as well.' [19]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Outbuildings were destroyed; a house had a large section of roofing torn off; another home sustained siding damage.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF0, SW of Watertown, Jefferson, WI (Watertown #1) – 'Trees were damaged, outbuildings were destroyed, and a house had a large section of roofing torn off. Another home sustained siding damage as well.' [20][13]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Houses were damaged; one home had a tree fall through its roof.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF1, SE of Watertown to NNE of Sullivan, Jefferson, WI (Watertown #2) – 'This tornado caused considerable damage to trees, outbuildings, and houses in and around the small community of Concord. ... One tree fell through the roof of a home.' [21][13]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: A small airplane hangar had its door torn off.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF0, NW of Farmington, Jefferson, WI – 'Trees and tree limbs were downed, and a small airplane hangar had its door torn off by this brief, weak tornado.' [22][13]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: A house was damaged by falling trees.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF1, W of Dousman, Jefferson, Waukesha, WI (Dousman #1) – 'Trees and tree branches were downed. One large tree fell on a house and others brought down power lines.' [23][24][13]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Part of a dock was thrown into the second floor of a home, causing damage.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF1, N of Dousman, Waukesha, WI – 'The tornado struck a small lake where it sunk boats and flipped docks. Part of a dock was thrown 150 ft into the second floor of a home, and additional trees and tree limbs were downed before the tornado dissipated.' [25][13]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Two barns were unroofed, a garage was destroyed, and a chimney was toppled.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF0, NE of Cochranton, Crawford, PA – 'A brief tornado unroofed two barns, destroyed a garage and blew it into a field, toppled a chimney, and blew a semi-truck off a road.' [28]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Barns, garages, and outbuildings were damaged or destroyed.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF1, Saltlick Township, Fayette, Westmoreland, PA – 'Barns, garages, and outbuildings were damaged or destroyed by this tornado. Damage to roofs and trees occurred as well.' [30][31]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Conservation buildings were damaged when trees fell on them.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF1, Laurel Hill State Park, Somerset, PA – 'Numerous trees were snapped or uprooted. Some trees fell onto conservation buildings, causing damage.' [32]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: At Northern Lehigh High School, the roof of a wooden dugout was torn off and metal bleachers were tossed; at Slatington Airport, an airplane hangar door was blown out and a small plane was tossed.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF1, Slatington, Lehigh, PA – 'Several trees were snapped or uprooted as the tornado touched down at Northern Lehigh High School. The roof of a wooden dugout at the school's baseball field was torn off, and some metal bleachers were tossed. The tornado continued east to the Slatington Airport, where an airplane hangar door was blown out and a small plane was tossed.' [35]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: A shed was destroyed; a few homes and other structures were damaged, including a house that lost much of its roof.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF2, New Athens, Harrison, OH – 'This tornado caused considerable damage in and around New Athens, where a shed was completely swept away and destroyed with only the concrete foundation remaining. A few homes and other structures in town were damaged, including a house that lost much of its roof.' [36]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: A farm home sustained broken windows and a toppled chimney; a metal shed was destroyed.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF2, ENE of Carrollton to SW of Salineville, OH – 'A strong tornado cut a path of severe tree damage through a large wooded area, and one hillside was completely deforested, with many large trees snapped or uprooted. A farm home sustained broken windows and a toppled chimney. Crops were damaged, and a metal shed was destroyed as well.' [37]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: A BJ's store had a section of its wall facade removed.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF0, Columbia, Howard, MD – 'A brief tornado struck the Snowden Square shopping mall along Snowden River Parkway, where a BJ's store had a section of its wall facade removed, and shopping carts were lofted and thrown.' [38]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: One house was damaged by falling trees and a power line.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF1, Western Bergholz, Jefferson, OH – 'This tornado downed numerous trees outside of town, and one house was damaged by falling trees and a power line.' [39]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Sheet metal roofing was ripped from a barn; a wooden 2x4 punctured the exterior wall of a metal shed.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF0, E of Indiana, Indiana, PA – 'A very small and brief tornado ripped sheet metal roofing from a barn and tossed the pieces downwind. Minor crop damage occurred, and a wooden 2x4 was thrown and punctured through the exterior wall of a metal shed.' [41]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: A large outbuilding was destroyed; a single-story home sustained roof damage; two barns were destroyed.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF0, NE of New Holland, Pickaway, OH – 'A large outbuilding was destroyed and a single story home sustained roof damage. Two barns were also destroyed.' [42]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: A barn was heavily damaged with some walls collapsed; several greenhouses were damaged.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF1, N of Gardenville to SW of Mechanicsville, Bucks, PA – 'A barn was heavily damaged with some walls collapsed. Trees and crops were damaged along the path, and several greenhouses were damaged as well.' [44]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: One single‐family home sustained destruction of its attached garage and partial roof loss; other homes sustained minor to moderate roof damage; in all, one business, one church, and 23 homes were damaged.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF1, Wintersville, Jefferson, OH – 'In Wintersville, one single‐family home sustained destruction of its attached garage and had partial loss of its roof, while other homes sustained minor to moderate roof damage. Extensive tree and fence damage was also observed, and a wooden 2x4 was found lodged into the exterior wall of a church. Metal roofing and signs were damaged as well. One business, one church, and 23 homes were damaged in the Wintersville area.' [45][46]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: One home was left severely damaged by a fallen tree.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF0, Verona, Essex, NJ – 'Several trees and large limbs were knocked down, with one home left severely damaged by a fallen tree.' [47]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Power poles were left leaning and debris from a nearby building was found in the power lines.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF1, S of Palestine, Crawford, IL – 'Power poles were left leaning with power lines down. Debris from a nearby building was found in the power lines.' [60]
EF0, ENE of Greenup, Cumberland, IL – 'Trees, crops, and a small outbuilding were damaged.' [52]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: A Montessori School had a portion of its roofing material torn off.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF1, Windsor, Mercer, NJ – 'A Montessori School in town had a portion of its roofing material torn off. Numerous trees were snapped or uprooted as well.' [53]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Several car dealership buildings sustained severe structural damage; one building largely collapsed; multiple mobile homes were damaged (with one completely destroyed); seven warehouse buildings were damaged; a small utility building lost its roof; and several site‐built homes, a church, a hotel, Walmart, Home Depot, and Lowe's sustained minor damage.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF3, Somerton to Bensalem, Philadelphia, Bucks, PA – 'A rain‐wrapped low‐end EF3 tornado caused major damage in the northeastern suburbs of Philadelphia, with the most intense damage occurring in Trevose and Bensalem. Several car dealership buildings sustained severe structural damage, with loss of roofs and exterior walls, and one building that largely collapsed. Many vehicles were flipped, thrown, or damaged by flying debris, and a large HVAC unit was thrown 200 yd. A storage trailer near one of the dealerships was lofted and dropped into an adjacent mobile home park, where multiple mobile homes were damaged, and one was completely destroyed. Seven warehouse buildings were damaged at an industrial park, one significantly, and a small utility building lost its roof. Several site‐built homes, a church, a hotel, Walmart, Home Depot, and Lowe's sustained minor damage as well.' [54][55][56]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: An apartment complex and other buildings sustained minor roof and siding damage; one building had ceiling panels pulled downward and insulation removed from a car park area.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF0, Bustleton, Philadelphia, PA – 'A brief, weak tornado touched down in the Bustleton neighborhood of Northeast Philadelphia. An apartment complex and other buildings sustained minor roof and siding damage. One building had ceiling panels pulled downward, and insulation was removed from a car park area.' [57]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Support beams on a porch were damaged, a masonry wall was knocked down, and an antenna pole was snapped.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF1, SE of Shelbyville to W of Waldron, Shelby, IN – 'Numerous trees were damaged, support beams on a porch were damaged, a masonry wall was knocked down, and an antenna pole was snapped.' [58]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: One building was damaged on the immediate western shore of Barnegat Bay; multiple houses sustained partial to total roof loss; one house had a wooden 2x4 speared through its exterior wall.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: EF2, Barnegat to Barnegat Light, Ocean, NJ – 'One building was damaged on the immediate western shore of Barnegat Bay as the tornado first developed. It moved over the bay as a waterspout. The waterspout became a tornado once again as it made landfall in High Bar Harbor, west of Barnegat Light. Multiple houses sustained partial to total roof loss, a car was moved, and some boats were flipped, moved, or damaged. Homes also had broken windows, siding stripped off, and damage to porches and sunrooms. A wooden 2x4 was speared through the exterior wall of one house, and a boat trailer was thrown 50 ft. Many trees and power poles were also snapped along the path.' [63]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: 4 deaths– This long‐tracked tornado began in White County, where a mobile home was destroyed, injuring three people.[2] In Jackson County, the worst damage occurred in Jacksonport; two people were killed by a falling tree, and a third death was in a destroyed mobile home. Several mobile and frame homes had their roofs partly torn off, and numerous trees were downed or sheared off along the path.[2] In Independence County, the tornado also damaged many homes and downed trees.[2] In Craighead County, one home was damaged, injuring two people inside.[2] In Lawrence County, 13 homes and other structures, including a grain bin storing rice, were damaged. Two people were injured as their mobile home rolled over.[2] In Greene County, one person was killed as the tornado damaged or destroyed 20 homes and other buildings. The worst damage in Greene County was in Marmaduke, which was later hit by an F3 tornado in 2006.[2]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: 15 deaths– Developing nearBenton, this tornado passed south of Bauxite andBryant before striking Vimy Ridge, killing 10 people in Saline County. The Shannon Hills area was devastated, reporting F4 damage; 90 homes were destroyed and 175 homes were damaged. Nearby, a home improvement center was completely destroyed south of Little Rock.[2][3] It then entered Pulaski County and struck the southern and eastern portions of the Little Rock suburbs, killing five people and injuring nearly 200 others before it lifted near Adams Field Airport in College Station.[2][3]The storm traveled for about 27 miles and had a maximum width of .8 miles.
